newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen moving in line with yen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen moving in line with yen.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to move largely in line with the yen on Thursday, with intensifying talks of a takeover of the Kia Group boosting buying of Kia Motors, brokers said.
"The yen's direction should be closely watched," said Lee Young-won of Daewoo Securities.

The composite index ended 5.79 points lower at 726.89 on Wednesday. "But Kia shares, including Kia Motors and Asia Motors are expected to fare well because a third-pary takeover emerges as the most likely solution to the Kia crisis," said Na Min-ho of Daishin Securities.
Brokers said there might be a rebound focused on shares that dropped sharply in recent days, including POSCO.
"But that will be technical. I am afraid the market needs to consolidate further before a solid recovery can take place," said Lee Moo-il of LG Securities.
Brokers said low levels of customer deposits with securities houses and tightening liquidity were dampening overall sentiment.
